original_question: Fix k >= 2 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G is F_{2k+1}-free or F_{2k+2}-free, must lambda(G) be at most (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1)) / 2, with equality only for K_k joined with an independent set of size m/k - (k - 1)/2?
target_in_paper: Section 3, in the subsection/paragraph on “Friendship graphs F_{k,3} and Fan graphs F_t,” most closely the fan-graph conjectural discussion represented in the survey by Conjectures 3.39–3.41. Your draft is aiming at the fan-graph extremal question with the bound (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1))/2 and extremal join graph K_k ∨ ((m/k) - (k - 1)/2)K_1. ([themoonlight.io](https://www.themoonlight.io/en/review/a-survey-of-edge-spectral-turn-type-problems-in-spectral-graph-theory-results-conjectures-and-open-problems))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the main spectral inequality, the forbidden-family shape F_{2k+1}/F_{2k+2}, the quantifiers k ≥ 2 and “m sufficiently large,” and the candidate extremal graph K_k ∨ ((m/k) - (k - 1)/2)K_1. Those are exactly the core ingredients of the fan-graph extremal problem discussed in the survey and quoted explicitly in later fan-graph papers. ([themoonlight.io](https://www.themoonlight.io/en/review/a-survey-of-edge-spectral-turn-type-problems-in-spectral-graph-theory-results-conjectures-and-open-problems))
missing_details: Define the forbidden graph family: F_t should be identified as the fan graph F_t := K_1 ∨ P_{t-1}, otherwise the notation can be confused with the friendship-graph notation used nearby in the survey. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.15918))

Specify that λ(G) is the spectral radius of the adjacency matrix of G. ([themoonlight.io](https://www.themoonlight.io/en/review/a-survey-of-edge-spectral-turn-type-problems-in-spectral-graph-theory-results-conjectures-and-open-problems))

State the ambient graph class explicitly: G should be a simple graph with exactly m edges; the survey uses the notation 𝒢(m,F) for F-free graphs of size m and notes that isolated vertices are irrelevant. ([themoonlight.io](https://www.themoonlight.io/en/review/a-survey-of-edge-spectral-turn-type-problems-in-spectral-graph-theory-results-conjectures-and-open-problems))

Define “F-free” as “containing no subgraph isomorphic to F.” ([themoonlight.io](https://www.themoonlight.io/en/review/a-survey-of-edge-spectral-turn-type-problems-in-spectral-graph-theory-results-conjectures-and-open-problems))
Clarify “for all sufficiently large m” as: for each fixed k, there exists m_0(k) such that the statement is asserted for all m ≥ m_0(k).
Make explicit the integrality condition for the claimed equality graph to exist: m - k(k-1)/2 must be divisible by k, equivalently (m/k) - (k - 1)/2 must be a nonnegative integer.

To be fully faithful to the survey’s Section 3 framing, note that the fan-graph discussion is residue-class sensitive: the survey points to separate conjectures for different modulo cases, so the plain join K_k ∨ ((m/k) - (k - 1)/2)K_1 corresponds to the residue class in which that graph actually exists. ([themoonlight.io](https://www.themoonlight.io/en/review/a-survey-of-edge-spectral-turn-type-problems-in-spectral-graph-theory-results-conjectures-and-open-problems))
If the word “or” is retained, it should be clear that the same extremal question is being asked separately for F_{2k+1}-free graphs and for F_{2k+2}-free graphs.
refined_question: Let F_t := K_1 ∨ P_{t-1} be the fan graph on t vertices, and let λ(G) denote the spectral radius of the adjacency matrix of a simple graph G with m edges (equivalently, G is taken from the survey’s edge-spectral setting 𝒢(m,F), so isolated vertices are ignored). Fix k ≥ 2. For all sufficiently large m in the residue class for which (m/k) - (k - 1)/2 is an integer, if G is F_{2k+1}-free or F_{2k+2}-free, must one have λ(G) ≤ (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1))/2, with equality if and only if G ≅ K_k ∨ ((m/k) - (k - 1)/2)K_1? ([themoonlight.io](https://www.themoonlight.io/en/review/a-survey-of-edge-spectral-turn-type-problems-in-spectral-graph-theory-results-conjectures-and-open-problems))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting the survey’s fan-graph discussion: the forbidden graphs are fans, the spectral bound is exactly the standard fan-graph threshold, and the proposed extremal graph is the same join graph that appears throughout the relevant fan-graph literature. The survey summary locates this material in Section 3 under the joint discussion of friendship graphs and fan graphs, and it also indicates that the survey’s actual presentation is sharpened into residue-class-specific conjectures (Conjectures 3.39–3.41), with Theorem 3.48 later unifying part of that picture. So the draft is mathematically close, but not fully stand-alone or fully paper-faithful until one adds the definition of the fan graph, the meaning of λ(G), the ambient class 𝒢(m,F), and the integrality/residue-class condition under which the stated equality graph exists. ([themoonlight.io](https://www.themoonlight.io/en/review/a-survey-of-edge-spectral-turn-type-problems-in-spectral-graph-theory-results-conjectures-and-open-problems))
